Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SurvFitSummary 2.2.1

The look of the Word report is closer to the template of the report:

  • The title and the subtitle are dark red (template of the package).
  • The placeholders of the overview for the items not given (data and outcome) are highlighted in yellow.
  • The Kaplan-Meier curves and the smoothed empirical hazards are given as a set of figures without confidence intervals followed by a set with them.
  • The overview gives the reporting interval as “Time intervals for reporting”.
  • In the plots of the spline models, the standard parametric model with the lowest AIC comes last in the legend.

Plots:

  • plot_survival_fits() and plot_hazard_fits() list the models in the legend in the order given in models (they followed the order of the fits).
  • With one arm, the row of the numbers at risk below the plots of plot_km() and plot_survival_fits() is labelled “N at risk”, without a title above it.

SurvFitSummary 2.2.0

The Word report follows the example figures of the report template more closely:

  • The plots of the smoothed empirical hazard with all the standard parametric models, and with the spline models, show the confidence interval of the smoothed hazard when the report includes figures with confidence intervals (the default).
  • The plots of the spline models also show the standard parametric model with the lowest AIC of the same fit (dashed line), and the plots of the Kaplan-Meier curve with the spline models mark the range of the predicted survival at 5 and 10 years.
  • The methods of the proportional hazards assessment are listed as bullet points, with the new style “List Bullet” of the template of the package (inst/templates/report_template.docx).
  • The quantile-quantile plot is shown at the same scale as the other figures, so that its text has the same size.

Plots:

  • New argument range_times of plot_survival_fits(): times at which a vertical line marks the range of the survival of the models plotted, labelled in percent.
  • plot_qq_survival() draws the identity and least-squares lines as segments, so that their keys in the legend are horizontal lines (they were diagonal).

SurvFitSummary 2.1.0

  • New reporting_times(): the reporting interval, the landmark times and the time horizon of write_survival_workbook() and write_survival_report(), with their defaults filled in, so that tables, predictions and plots made with the other functions can use the same times (for example in the Shiny app of the package). The workbook and the report now take these times from reporting_times(); their contents are unchanged.

SurvFitSummary 2.0.0

Version 2.0.0 redesigns the package: the functions of version 1.0.0 are replaced by those below.

  • processing_dataset() keeps covariate and stratification columns (column_covariates, column_strata), returns ARM as a factor with the control arm (control_arm) as the first level, checks that the times are positive and that the indicator contains only 0 and 1, removes rows with missing values with a warning, and also reads SAS transport (.xpt) files. CSV files are read with utils::read.csv().
  • generate_dummy_survival_data() restores the random number generator state of the session (the simulated values are unchanged).
  • New summarise_data(): numbers of patients, events and censored observations, and the median with its confidence interval, by arm.
  • New km_table(): Kaplan-Meier estimates with standard errors and confidence intervals, and the numbers at risk, events and censored observations at regular times.
  • New estimate_hazard_ratio(): hazard ratios from unadjusted, adjusted, unstratified and stratified Cox models, with the control arm as the reference (in version 1.0.0 the reference arm of the Cox model did not follow control_arm).
  • New test_proportional_hazards(): Grambsch-Therneau test of proportional hazards.
  • New estimate_empirical_hazard(): smoothed empirical hazard by arm with bshazard::bshazard().
  • New fit_survival_models() replaces fitting_surv_mod() and fitting_surv_mod_multiple(): fits all the parametric and Royston-Parmar spline models once, for each arm and for both arms with the arm as a covariate, and returns an object of class survfitsummary used by all the tables. Twelve distributions are available (exponential, Weibull in the accelerated failure time and proportional hazards forms, Rayleigh, lognormal, log-logistic, Gompertz, gamma, generalized gamma and generalized F, each also in its original parameterisation); the default is the seven standard models of NICE DSU TSD 14. Spline models on the hazard, odds and normal scales with 1 to 3 knots at quantiles of the log event times or at times given by the user. A model that fails or warns is recorded with its message and the other models are still fitted; the optimiser uses a smaller tolerance (reltol = 1e-10) and, for the spline models on the normal scale, whose gradient flexsurv computes numerically, a smaller step of the numerical gradient (ndeps = 1e-5). Print-ready model names (for example “Log-logistic”, “Generalized Gamma”, “Hazards, 2 knots”).
  • summary() and plot() methods for the fitted models: summary() gives the fit statistics and the status of all the models, including those that failed, and plot() calls plot_survival_fits() (type = "survival") or plot_hazard_fits() (type = "hazard"), by default for the models of the control arm.
  • New parameter_table(): estimates, standard errors and confidence intervals on the natural and transformed scales.
  • New covariance_table(): covariance matrices and their lower triangular Cholesky factors on the transformed and natural (delta method) scales (in version 1.0.0 the Cholesky factor was upper triangular).
  • New gof_table(): log-likelihood, AIC and BIC sorted by AIC; the fixed shape of the Rayleigh model is not counted.
  • New predict_survival(): survival, hazard or cumulative hazard at given times for each arm, with simulated confidence limits (seed, without changing the random number generator of the session) and the Kaplan-Meier estimate, NA after the largest observed time of the arm.
  • New survival_summary(): median, mean and restricted mean survival.
  • New spline_knot_table(): placement of the knots with the number at risk and the Kaplan-Meier estimate at each knot.
  • New plots, replacing plot_km_and_parametric(), plot_km_and_parametric_multiple(), plot_hazard_and_parametric(), plot_hazard_and_parametric_multiple(), plot_test_ph_assumption(), plot_schoenfeld() and plot_qq_survival() of version 1.0.0. They draw from the fitted object, so plots with and without confidence bands do not refit the models, use print-ready model names with the AIC in the legend, start the axes at (0, 0), and place the legend with legend_position (below the plot by default, with the models of one arm in two columns). colours and linetypes set the colours and line types of the arms, curves or elements of a plot, and text_sizes the font sizes of the titles, axes, legend and numbers at risk; by default the plots keep the colours, line types and font sizes of the report.
    • plot_km(): Kaplan-Meier curves with numbers at risk; each curve ends at the largest observed time of its arm (in version 1.0.0 the curves were extended to the longest arm).
    • plot_empirical_hazard(): smoothed empirical hazard without fitted models.
    • plot_survival_fits() and plot_hazard_fits(): Kaplan-Meier curve or smoothed empirical hazard with the fitted parametric and spline models, extrapolated to a time horizon, for one arm with several models or one model with several arms (independent or dependent fits).
    • plot_distribution_diagnostics(): log(-log S(t)), log-odds and probit of the Kaplan-Meier estimate against log time, and the log of the smoothed hazard against time (in version 1.0.0 the Gompertz plot used log(-log S(t)) against time, which is not linear for the Gompertz).
    • plot_schoenfeld(): the reference line is the estimated log hazard ratio, around which the scaled residuals are centred (it was 0 in version 1.0.0), and the regression on time is a natural spline with its confidence interval as in survival::plot.cox.zph().
    • plot_qq_survival(): the axes are set from the data (they were fixed at 0 to 100 in version 1.0.0).
  • New write_survival_workbook(): Excel workbook with one table per sheet (data summary, Kaplan-Meier table, hazard ratios, proportional hazards test, model status, fit statistics, parameters on the natural and transformed scales with the rows of their covariance matrix, covariance matrices and Cholesky factors, survival summary, predicted survival and knots), with print-ready model names.
  • New write_survival_report(): Word report on the extrapolation of survival data for health technology assessment (overview, methods, data overview, diagnostics, standard parametric models and spline-based extrapolation for each arm and for both arms), with figures without and with confidence intervals, smoothed hazard plots without fitted models, and print-ready model names. The styles come from a template in the package (inst/templates/report_template.docx: A4, Arial, numbered headings), or from a document given in template. Replaces the Word export of the Shiny application of version 1.0.0.
  • New example dataset inst/extdata/fit_example.csv (two arms of 300 patients) and independent reference values for the tests (inst/validation/python/expected_fits.py, numpy and scipy).
  • Validation and reproduction scripts: inst/validation/ compares the package with closed forms, survival::survreg(), rstpm2::stpm2() and the Python reference, checks the Excel workbook and the Word report, and estimates the coverage of the confidence intervals by simulation; inst/reproduce/ reproduces published results of Jackson (2016) and Royston and Parmar (2002). Every comparison is also run with the values of the package shifted (inst/validation/run_validation.R).
  • Three vignettes (getting started, the parametric and spline models, and the validation) and a pkgdown website.
  • The license is GPL (>= 2) instead of MIT.
  • broom, dplyr, magrittr, purrr, readr, rlang, tibble and tidyr are no longer used; flexsurv (>= 2.3), ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0), grDevices, officer, patchwork, splines and writexl are imported; haven, readxl, xml2, knitr and rmarkdown (for the vignettes) are suggested packages.

SurvFitSummary 1.0.0

Initial Release (2025-11-30)

This is the first official release of SurvFitSummary, a comprehensive R package for parametric survival model fitting and diagnostic visualization.

Major Features

Data Processing
  • processing_dataset(): Flexible data processing function supporting multiple formats (CSV, Excel, SAS)
    • Automatic column mapping for ARM, SURVTIME, EVENT/CNSR
    • Support for both event (EVENT=1) and censoring (CNSR=1) indicators
    • Input validation and error handling
Dummy Data Generation
  • generate_dummy_survival_data(): Generate simulated survival data for testing
    • Supports multiple treatment arms
    • Exponential event time generation with specified hazard rates
    • Administrative censoring and dropout handling
    • Reproducible results with seed parameter
Model Fitting Functions
  • fitting_surv_mod(): Fit single parametric distribution
    • Seven parametric distributions: exponential, Weibull, lognormal, log-logistic, Gompertz, generalized gamma, gamma
    • Dependent (covariate) and independent (stratified) model options
    • Parameter estimates with confidence intervals
    • Variance-covariance and Cholesky decomposition matrices
    • Goodness-of-fit statistics (AIC, BIC)
    • Landmark survival probabilities
    • Survival metrics (median, mean, RMST)
    • Time scale conversion support
  • fitting_surv_mod_multiple(): Fit and compare multiple distributions
    • Batch fitting of multiple distributions
    • Support for both dependent and independent models simultaneously
    • Standardized time scale handling (day, week, month, year)
    • Cox proportional hazards model results for comparison
    • Comprehensive output combining all model results
Kaplan-Meier Visualization
  • plot_km_and_parametric(): KM curves with single parametric overlay
    • Kaplan-Meier step curves
    • Parametric distribution smooth curves
    • Optional 95% confidence intervals
    • Number at risk table
    • Automatic axis scaling
  • plot_km_and_parametric_multiple(): KM curves with multiple parametric overlays
    • Faceted plots by distribution
    • Consistent color scheme across panels
    • Shared axes for easy comparison
    • Support for 2+ treatment arms
Hazard Function Visualization
  • plot_hazard_and_parametric(): Hazard plots with single distribution
    • Non-parametric hazard estimation (bshazard)
    • Parametric hazard curves with 95% CI
    • Support for multiple treatment arms
  • plot_hazard_and_parametric_multiple(): Hazard plots with multiple distributions
    • Faceted comparison of hazard functions
    • Consistent visualization across distributions
    • Easy identification of hazard patterns
Diagnostic Plots
  • plot_schoenfeld(): Scaled Schoenfeld residuals
    • Test proportional hazards assumption
    • LOESS smoothing curves
    • Beta coefficient and p-value annotations
    • Support for multiple treatment comparisons
    • Faceted display for 3+ arms
  • plot_test_ph_assumption(): Complementary log-log and related plots
    • Four diagnostic plots: log(-log(S)) vs log(t), log(-log(S)) vs t, Φ⁻¹(S) vs log(t), Φ⁻¹(S) vs t
    • Parallel curves indicate proportional hazards
    • Faceted layout for easy comparison
  • plot_qq_survival(): Q-Q plots for survival distributions
    • Compare survival time distributions between arms
    • Identity line and regression fit with 95% CI
    • Faceted plots for 3+ arms vs control
    • Quantile-based comparison

Technical Features

  • Full roxygen2 documentation for all functions
  • Comprehensive examples in function documentation
  • Input validation and informative error messages
  • Consistent API design across functions
  • Support for factor and character ARM variables
  • Automatic handling of reference group specification
  • Non-ASCII character compliance for CRAN compatibility
  • No global variable warnings (proper NSE handling)

Dependencies

  • Core: R (>= 4.0.0)
  • Survival Analysis: survival, flexsurv, bshazard
  • Data Manipulation: dplyr, tidyr, tibble, purrr
  • Visualization: ggplot2, patchwork
  • Data Import: readr, readxl, haven
  • Utilities: broom, rlang, magrittr, stats

Supported Distributions

  1. Exponential ("exp")
  2. Weibull ("weibull")
  3. Lognormal ("lnorm")
  4. Log-logistic ("llogis")
  5. Gompertz ("gompertz")
  6. Generalized Gamma ("gengamma")
  7. Gamma ("gamma")

Output Components

All model fitting functions return comprehensive results including: * Parameter estimates with standard errors and confidence intervals * Variance-covariance matrices (full and Cholesky decomposition) * Goodness-of-fit statistics for model comparison * Landmark survival probabilities at specified time points * Survival metrics (median, mean, RMST) with time scale conversion * Cox PH model results (in fitting_surv_mod_multiple())

Quality Assurance

  • Passes R CMD check with 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
  • All functions fully documented with roxygen2
  • Consistent coding style and naming conventions
  • Proper handling of edge cases (single arm, missing data, etc.)
  • Informative messages and warnings for users

Known Limitations

  • Generalized gamma distribution may require larger sample sizes for stable parameter estimation
  • Time scale conversion assumes linear relationship (appropriate for survival time units)
  • Non-parametric hazard estimation (bshazard) may be sensitive to bandwidth selection

Future Development

Planned features for future releases: * Additional parametric distributions (e.g., piecewise exponential, spline-based) * Model averaging and ensemble methods * Extrapolation diagnostics * Interactive Shiny application * Bayesian parameter estimation options * Additional goodness-of-fit tests

For bug reports and feature requests, please visit: https://github.com/gosukehommaEX/SurvFitSummary/issues
